shape: small things you did without thinking as a kid that take nerve now, each told as what you did, never as advice

slides.text: how brave we used to be between nine and three
raising your hand straight in the air before you even had [[the rest of the sentence]] ready.
standing up in front of thirty desks to read three shaky lines you wrote about a stray dog.
walking straight up to the big wooden desk just to say "i don't get it".
leaving a grey pebble from the gravel yard on the corner of the chalk tray, certain it was safe.
crying over a torn workbook page by the metal pencil sharpener, without once hiding your face.
handing over a lopsided picture of your family, [[never doubting]] it belonged taped flat to the blackboard.
save this for a morning you hesitate, and remember the teacher who gave you that nerve.

caption:
nobody is born second-guessing what they have to say.
we only felt that brave because one good teacher made thirty desks feel safe.
save this for a morning you hesitate before speaking up.
